**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a non-buffering logger as the default**

Falling back to `new MemoryLogger()` here makes the server buffer every log entry in an unbounded in-memory array whenever the caller does not pass `config.logger`. In real deployments that omit custom logging, this causes steady memory growth and eventual instability/OOM under normal traffic; a no-op or bounded logger should be the default instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve metadata response contract for missing metadata**

Returning `ok(meta)` now emits `data: null` when a bot has no stored metadata, but SDK callers are still typed/implemented against a metadata object shape (for example `recfn/client/src/resources/metadata.ts` returns `ApiResult<MeetingMetadata>`). This creates a runtime contract break where existing consumers can dereference metadata fields and crash; either keep a non-null placeholder response or update client contracts in lockstep.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow participant frames without consent field**

The new frame validator rejects `participant_joined` payloads unless `consent` is present, but the worker path still explicitly accounts for adapters omitting consent (it later defaults to `pending` in `server/src/worker/bot-worker.ts`). In that scenario, `createFrame('participant_joined', ...)` now throws and the join-event flow fails instead of streaming the participant update; the parser should accept missing consent (or default it) to match producer behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
